title: Flower Atlas Image Credits
text: Flower Atlas Image Credits The reference photos in the bouquet review ("Looks like") come from the platform's flower atlas. We use only images we may use commercially, and we credit every one of them. Where the images come from Wikimedia Commons — files under CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA. The credit follows Commons’ suggested form: Author, licence, via Wikimedia Commons, with a link to the file page. iNaturalist — research-grade observations whose photos are CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA. The credit is the photo’s own attribution, via iNaturalist, with a link to the photo. Our own photos, and photos from partner florists or growers given to us with written permission. We never use Google Images or any other source without a clear licence, and never images under non-commercial (NC) or no-derivatives (ND) licences. Every image is checked by our team before any florist sees it. The current list The live list of every published image, with its author, licence and source link, is public: in the Vendor Portal: Image credits in the page footer (/Atlas/Attributions, no sign-in needed); as data: GET https://api.findmyflowers.pl/api/v1/atlas/attributions. In the review, hover over a “Looks like” picture to see its credit, or click it to open the source page. Licences Licence What it allows What we must do CC0 1.0 Any use Nothing (we still name the source) CC BY 4.0 (and older versions) Any use, including commercial Credit the author, link the licence, say if we changed the image (we resize it) CC BY-SA 4.0 (and older versions) Any use, including commercial As CC BY; our resized copy is shared under the same licence Found a problem with an image or its credit? Write to contact@findmyflowers.pl and we’ll fix or remove it.

title: User Manuals
text: # User Manuals Step-by-step visual guides for each portal and app of the FlowerShop IoT Platform. Each manual is a self-contained HTML file with embedded screenshots — open it directly in any browser, no internet connection required. ## Portal & App Manuals 🛡️ Admin Portal Manual Complete guide for platform administrators — manage vendors & approvals, subscriptions, vase orders, asset-recovery incidents, customers, orders and payments at admin.findmyflowers.pl 🌹 Vendor Portal Manual Complete guide for flower shop owners and freelance florists — self sign-up, dashboard, bouquets, live vase status, vase ordering, orders, stock, payments, analytics, billing and settings at vendors.findmyflowers.pl 📱 Vendor Mobile App Manual Guide to the FindMyFlowers Business Android app — sign-up, photographing and pricing bouquets at the vase, QR scanning, vase status, orders, alerts, customer bouquet requests, stock (incl. counting from photos) and the AI Florist 📘 Customer App Manual Complete guide for customers — discover bouquets on the map, manage your cart, place orders and track deliveries at app.findmyflowers.pl ## Coverage | Manual | Screenshots | Sections | Theme | |--------|-------------|----------|-------| | Admin Portal | 23 pages | Authentication, Dashboard, Vendor Mgmt, Vase Mgmt, Customer Mgmt, Orders, Payments, **Subscriptions**, **Vendor Approval**, **Vase Order Fulfillment**, **Asset Recovery** | Blue | | Vendor Portal | 30 pages | Authentication, Self Sign-Up, Dashboard, Bouquets, Smart Vases (online / offline), Vase Ordering, Orders, **Stock**, Payments, Feedback, Analytics, Settings, Billing, Support | Green | | Vendor Mobile App | 87 screens | Getting Started, **Native Sign-Up**, Home, Smart Vases & QR, Bouquets & Map, Orders, Alerts, **Stock & counting from photos**, **AI Florist** (start from stock, reconstruct, cost assessor, ratings & refine, house style), Business Settings (**how you sell**), Vase Ordering, Insights, Billing, **Help**, **Bouquet Requests** | Green | | Customer App | 11 pages | Browse Bouquets, Authentication, Shopping, Orders, Account | Teal | > Sections in **bold** for the Admin Portal cover the EP-19–22 features (vendor self-registration, SaaS platform subscription, smart-vase hardware ordering, and asset-recovery incidents); for the vendor manuals they mark the newest features (EP-28 AI Florist, EP-30 / EP-M11 stock management, native mobile sign-up). The vendor manuals are generated from `scripts/manuals/*.json` with `python scripts/manuals/build_manual.py `; screenshots live in `docs/manuals/screenshots/vendor` and `vendor-mobile`.

title: Use-case Flows
text: # Use-case Flows Four illustrated walkthroughs of how people use FindMyFlowers, from the first idea to the bouquet in someone's hands. Each picture reads left to right along the top row, then right to left along the bottom row (steps 1–6). From a picture to your bouquet: a customer asks nearby florists for a bouquet From the flower shop to the map: an in-store florist sells a bouquet from a smart vase Sell flowers online, without a smart vase: an online-only florist sells a delivery-only bouquet From your stock to a bouquet with AI Florist: a florist designs a bouquet from their own stock ## From a picture to your bouquet *Customer + nearby florists (customer bouquet requests, EP-37)* ![From a picture to your bouquet: share your wish, nearby florists, AI helps the florist, compare offers, choose and pay, made and delivered]({{ '/assets/use-case-flows/01-customer-photo-request-to-bouquet.png' | relative_url }}) 1. **Share your wish.** The customer posts a request with one or more reference photos, a budget, the time they want it and a delivery address. 2. **Nearby florists.** Florists whose service area covers the address see the request on their map. They only see an approximate location (about 500 m) and no personal details. 3. **AI helps the florist.** The florist can reconstruct the bouquet from the photos with AI Florist: it recognises the flowers, matches them to the florist's stock and estimates the cost. The florist checks the result before using it. 4. **Compare offers.** The customer gets offers with a price, photos, delivery time and any substitution notes. 5. **Choose & pay.** The customer accepts one offer, and the other offers are declined automatically. Payment must be completed within 30 minutes, or the acceptance lapses. 6. **Made & delivered.** The florist sees the exact address only after payment, then makes and delivers the bouquet. The customer follows the progress with a countdown. AI assistance depends on the florist's setup, and florists always review its suggestions. ## From the flower shop to the map *In-store florist + customer (smart vases)* ![From the flower shop to the map: make the bouquet, choose a smart vase, set price and freshness, appear on the map, customer chooses and pays, prepare and hand over]({{ '/assets/use-case-flows/02-smart-vase-bouquet-to-map.png' | relative_url }}) 1. **Make the bouquet.** The florist makes a real arrangement in the shop. 2. **Choose a smart vase.** They place it in a smart vase and upload a photo of it in the Vendor Portal (or the vendor app). The vase shows a QR code that links to the bouquet. 3. **Set price & freshness.** They set the price and, optionally, a freshness promise of 1–3 days. 4. **Appear on the map.** The bouquet shows on the customer map at the shop's location while it is available and its vase is connected. 5. **Customer chooses & pays.** A customer picks the bouquet on the map, or by scanning the vase's QR code, and pays.
